sources.entry: GPT Migrate team is working on adding benchmarks for the agent

summary.one_liner: GPT-Migrate is a tool that uses LLMs to migrate a codebase from one framework or language to another, such as Flask/Python to Node.js, generating the new code, Docker environment, and unit tests.
summary.what_it_does: Takes a source directory and entrypoint, then uses an LLM (OpenRouter or OpenAI, default GPT-4-32k) to rebuild the code in a target language (e.g. --targetlang nodejs) into a target directory. It first creates a Docker environment for the target language, identifies third-party source dependencies and picks target equivalents, and recursively rewrites files starting from the entrypoint. It then runs the new app in Docker on a target port, writes Python unittest-based tests, optionally checks those tests against the running original app on a source port, and iteratively debugs the migrated code using logs and error messages. Steps can be run separately via --step setup, migrate, test, or all. The README notes that shell actions such as moving files require user confirmation.
use_cases: Migrate a Python Flask app to Node.js
Port a codebase from one framework to another
Rewrite a legacy project in a new language
Generate unit tests for a migrated REST API
Scaffold a Docker environment for a target language
how_to_run: Install Docker and make sure it is running
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<your key>  (or export OPENAI_API_KEY=<your key>)
notable: Multi-step pipeline: setup, migrate, test, and debug, runnable individually via --step
Optional validation of generated unit tests against the original running app via --sourceport
Prompt system organized into four preference levels (HIERARCHY, p1 to p4) that compose into prompts
Ships with a flask-nodejs benchmark app; default model gpt-4-32k
caveats: Alpha-stage software; the README says it is not yet ready for production use and should not be trusted blindly
Costs can add up quickly because it may rewrite an entire codebase; GPT-4-class models are recommended
Per the README, about 50% success on simple languages like Python or JavaScript, and complex languages like C++ or Rust need human help
keywords: migrate my app to a new language
